title: Rethinking Preventive Health to Generate Better Outcomes
what_it_is: Rethinking Preventive Health to Generate Better Outcomes

sections.label: Preventive healthcare spending share
sections.summary: Last year's preventive healthcare spending was about 5% of total non-COVID-19 MOH spending, with about $330 million allocated to HPB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our spending on preventive healthcare efforts last year was about 5% of total non-COVID-19 MOH spending, with about $330 million allocated to HPB.

sections.label: Chronic disease prevalence rates
sections.summary: About one in three residents aged 40 to 69 has hypertension and two in five have high cholesterol, with 2015 diabetes prevalence at about 11% versus the OECD average of 7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is true that our mortality rates for cancer, stroke and heart disease have improved, perhaps owing to technological and economic factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But as the Singapore Public Sector Outcomes Review does soberingly acknowledge, about one in three residents aged 40 to 69 has hypertension and two in five have high cholesterol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Based on the last like-for-like comparison I could find, our 2015 diabetes prevalence among those aged 20 to 79 at about 11% is much higher than the OECD average of 7%.

sections.label: Diabetes prevalence not decreased
sections.summary: MOH said at last year's Committee of Supply that diabetes prevalence has not decreased from 2017 to 2020, five years after Singapore declared war on diabetes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, although it has been five years since Singapore declared war on diabetes, MOH said at the Committee of Supply last year that "the prevalence of diabetes has not decreased" from 2017 to 2020.

sections.label: Flu vaccination take-up rates
sections.summary: Flu vaccination take-up among Singaporeans aged 65 and above is 24%, lower than about 70% in Australia, the UK and the US, with about 4,000 annual pneumonia and influenza deaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a reply to my earlier Parliamentary Question, the Government acknowledged that our take-up rate for flu vaccinations of 24% among Singaporeans aged 65 and above is significantly lower than the equivalent rate of about 70% in Australia, the UK and the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to one widely-cited figure, about 4,000 people in Singapore die from pneumonia and influenza every year.

sections.label: SFL subsidy take-up rate
sections.summary: 100,000 of 1.8 million eligible Singaporeans, or 5.6%, benefited from SFL subsidies, versus national health screening take-up of 22% in Japan and 30% in Taiwan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to MOH's response to a Parliamentary Question I filed, 100,000 out of 1.8 million of eligible Singaporeans, or 5.6%, have benefited from SFL subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By comparison, take-up rates of national health screening programmes are 22% in Japan and 30% in Taiwan, versus our 5.6%.

sections.label: Life expectancy education gap
sections.summary: MOH revealed the life expectancy gap between those with post-Secondary and above education versus below Secondary education was 5.8 years, and asked about preventive programmes and data release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In reply to my earlier Parliamentary Question in 2020, MOH revealed that the life expectancy gap between those with post-Secondary and above education versus those with below Secondary education was 5.8 years, basically, six years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How effective, though, are the existing preventive health care programmes targeted at low-income groups such as Healthy Living Passport, KidSTART and Propel?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can we release more data on chronic disease prevalence and other health outcomes by gender, by socio-economic status?

sections.label: Public diabetes data and patient records
sections.summary: A speaker asks for quarterly public diabetes data, precinct-level chronic disease data for MPs, and comprehensive patient data for healthcare providers with permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It would help us to have public data on diabetes, say, quarterly, to ensure not only better public debate on healthcare policy, but also better alignment of outcomes and incentives to providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And on this note, I would like to ask if all Members of Parliament can be given data on chronic disease patterns and also other relevant indicators at the precinct level in their wards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can we conclusively move towards a system where a comprehensive data on a patient is easily and always available to healthcare providers, assuming permissions are given, of course?

sections.label: NEHR access and AI automation
sections.summary: The speaker says NEHR data access is not easy or streamlined and suggests government investment in IT automation prompting doctors toward possible conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Right now, data is available from the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR), but feedback is that the process of accessing it is not easy and not streamlined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would also suggest that the Government invest more in workforce automation of sorts for doctors, such that the IT system prompts them towards possible conditions the patient may have or alternative theories based on data analytics and AI.

sections.label: Preventive healthcare challenges and ideas
sections.summary: The speaker says preventive healthcare challenges are large and complex with no single solution, but researched ideas for change exist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The challenges we face in preventive healthcare are large, complex and defy any one magic bullet, but there are good ideas for change on the table, ideas that have been researched and put to the test academically and in the experience of other countries.

sections.label: Primary Care 2.0 and GPs
sections.summary: In 2016 MOH introduced the Action Plan for Primary Care 2.0 to anchor GPs in chronic disease management.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In 2016, MOH put forth the Action Plan for Primary Care 2.0, to anchor the role of GPs in chronic disease management, a point which Mr Leon Perera has made, to make GPs the anchor.

sections.label: Screen for Life and cancer screening uptake
sections.summary: Screen for Life was introduced at over 1,100 CHAS GP clinics, yet 2020 NPHS data showed cancer screening uptake stayed between 40% and 50% for cervical, breast and colorectal cancers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For example, the national Screen for Life (SFL) programme was introduced across more than 1,100 CHAS GP clinics to provide easy access to affordable and appropriate screening for eligible persons for cardiovascular disease risk factors, such as diabetes, high blood pressure and high blood cholesterol, and also certain cancers, like cancers of the breast, cervix and colon/rectum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In fact, based on the National Population Health Survey (NPHS) done in 2020, despite efforts to make screening accessible and affordable for all, cancer screening uptake rates remained between only 40% and 50% for each of these three cancers: cervical, breast and colorectal.

sections.label: Free NCIS vaccinations for children
sections.summary: All recommended NCIS vaccinations are free for Singaporean children at polyclinics and CHAS GP clinics under VCDSS, supporting marriage and parenthood and cohort-based vaccination.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In fact, all recommended vaccinations under the National Childhood Immunisation Schedule (NCIS) are free for Singaporean children at polyclinics and CHAS GP clinics under the Vaccination and Child Development Screening Subsidies (VCDSS) as part of the Government's efforts to support marriage and parenthood and to encourage vaccinations on a cohort basis.

sections.label: HPV vaccine school programme
sections.summary: The HPV vaccine was introduced in the school health programme in 2019, with all Secondary 1 female students offered it fully subsidised in schools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For example, the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine that Mr Leon Perera talked about was actually introduced as a part of the school health programme in 2019 – a few years ago now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: And all cohorts of Secondary 1 female students are offered the fully subsidised HPV vaccine in their respective schools.

sections.label: HPB worker reach December 2021
sections.summary: As of end December 2021, HPB reached more than 1.24 million workers, with over 213,000 participating in virtual and face-to-face sessions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As of end December 2021, HPB has reached more than 1.24 million workers, with more than 213,000 workers participating in both virtual and face-to-face programme sessions.

sections.label: Programme exercise and health survey
sections.summary: Participants' daily exercise minutes rose over 39%, while the National Population Health Survey 2020 saw more hypertension, hyperlipidemia and less physical activity and screening.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The programme has encouraged participants to be more active, with their daily exercise minutes increased by over 39% when compared to the month before they started on the programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: While we have made progress over the years, the latest National Population Health Survey 2020 saw an increase in the prevalence of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and a reduction in the prevalence of Singaporeans with sufficient total physical activity and screening participation, partly due to the COVID-19 disruptions.

sections.label: MOH refining preventive health approach
sections.summary: MOH and relevant stakeholders will continually refine their approach to preventive health to bring about a healthier Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: MOH, together with relevant stakeholders, will also continually refine our approach to preventive health to bring about a healthier Singapore.
